evidence: src/auth/auth.service.ts: the session hash is built inline with `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex')` in `validateLogin`, `validateSocialLogin` and `refreshToken`. This rule has no single helper, unlike `getTokensData`.

src/auth/auth.service.ts: `register` and `update` both sign a confirm-email JWT with `jwtService.signAsync` using `auth.confirmEmailSecret` and `auth.confirmEmailExpires`. `confirmEmail` and `confirmNewEmail` both verify with the same secret and the same `confirmEmailUserId` payload key, and each repeats the same try/catch that throws `invalidHash`.

src/auth/auth.service.ts: `bcrypt.compare` is called directly in `validateLogin` and in `update` (old-password check). Each caller repeats the 'no stored password -> incorrect password' guard, so password verification has no single home.

src/auth/auth.service.ts: `getTokensData` centralises access and refresh token signing. `forgotPassword`, `register`, `update`, `confirmEmail` and `resetPassword` bypass it and call `jwtService` and `configService.getOrThrow` inline. Token creation and verification is therefore handled in two different styles in one class.
src/auth/auth.service.ts: the `UnprocessableEntityException({status: HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, errors: {...}})` construction is repeated about 15 times, with no shared helper.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: AuthService is cohesive in concern: every method is authentication or account-identity work. It fails on the "keep each rule or invariant in one place" criterion. The session-hash invariant is copied inline three times. The password-compare rule is copied twice. The email-confirmation token rule is split across four methods. Token handling is also inconsistent. `getTokensData` is a private helper for access and refresh tokens, but other JWT types are signed and verified inline with `jwtService` and config lookups.

violations.message: The session hash rule (sha256 of randomStringGenerator) is duplicated inline in validateLogin, validateSocialLogin and refreshToken. The confirm-email JWT sign/verify logic is duplicated across register, update, confirmEmail and confirmNewEmail. bcrypt.compare and its no-password guard are repeated in validateLogin and update. Only access and refresh tokens go through getTokensData, so token handling is inconsistent within the class.
